passages.original: 21. Ante Melchiadis ævum scripsit Tertullianus lib. de Corona, c. 3 : « Die Dominico jejunium nefas ducimus. > Legitur et ad calcem libri v apostolicarum Constitutionum : < Reus enim erit peccati, qui Dominico die jejunaverit,cum sit dies resurrectio- nis. > Nulla hic alia ratio subjicitur. Sed subinde I Augustinus, epist.
passages.english: 21. Before the age of Melchiades, Tertullian wrote in the book On the Crown, ch. 3: "On the Lord's day we consider fasting unlawful." And at the end of book 5 of the Apostolic Constitutions one reads: "For he will be guilty of sin who fasts on the Lord's day, since it is the day of the resurrection." No other reason is given here. But afterwards Augustine, letter
passages.notes: Stray 'I' before Augustinus treated as a footnote mark. The sentence continues in the following context (letter 36, to Casulanus).

passages.original: 2 prohibet, < ne quis jejunet die Dominica , causa temporis, aut persuasionis aut superstitionis, > jcjunium etiam die Dominico , modo absit superstitionis causa, permit- tere quodam modo videntur. Et Hieronymus quidem, epist. 28, ad Lucinium scribit: < Utinam omni tempore jejunare possimus : quod in Aclibus A postolorum (ut etiam Augustinus epist. 56, n. 28 , observavit) diebus Pentecostes et die Dominico aposlolum Paulum ct cum eo credentes iecisse legimus. » Ne hinc tamen Ecclesiæ morem ac legem improbare videatur, mox dictum temperans addit: < Nec hoc dico, quod Dominicis dicbus jejunandum putem.
passages.english: 2, forbids "that anyone fast on the Lord's day on account of the season, or of conviction, or of superstition," they seem in a certain way to permit fasting even on the Lord's day, provided the motive of superstition is absent. And Jerome indeed writes in letter 28, to Lucinius: "Would that we could fast at all times: as we read in the Acts of the Apostles (as Augustine also observed, letter 56, n. 28) that the apostle Paul and the believers with him did on the days of Pentecost and on the Lord's day." Yet lest he seem by this to reject the custom and law of the Church, he soon tempers what he said and adds: "Nor do I say this because I think one should fast on Lord's days.
passages.notes: The opening '2' is the end of a canon number begun in the preceding context (the canon of the Council of Saragossa); the clause's subject is the councils just mentioned. 'iecisse' read as 'fecisse' (did).

passages.original: Sane ab hoc die mœrori ac jejuniis consecrando, procul aberant pagani, quibus eumdem in honore Jovis feslivum agere solemne erat. Qnocirca christianos quosdam, quos ad perversam eorum imitationem diabolus seduxerat, Cæsarius Arelatensis episcopus , apud Augustinum, append. t. v, serm. 265, n. 5, vehementer corripit his verbis : < Quia audivimus quod aliquos viros vel mulieres ita diabolus circumveniat, ut quinta feria nec viri opera faciant, nec mulieres lanificium, coram Deo et sanctis angelis contestamur, quia quicumque hoc observare voluerint, nisi per prolixam et duram pœnitentiam tale sacrilegiumemendaverint, etc. > Eamdem rem concilium Narbonense, anno 589 habitum, quam indigne ferret, can.
passages.english: Certainly the pagans were far from consecrating this day to mourning and fasting, since it was their solemn custom to keep it as a festival in honour of Jupiter. For this reason Caesarius, bishop of Arles, in [the works of] Augustine, appendix to vol. 5, sermon 265, n. 5, sharply rebukes certain Christians whom the devil had seduced into a perverse imitation of them, in these words: "Because we have heard that the devil so deceives some men and women that on the fifth day of the week the men do no work and the women no wool-working, we solemnly declare before God and the holy angels that whoever wishes to observe this, unless they amend such sacrilege by long and hard penance, etc." The Council of Narbonne, held in the year 589, revealed how indignantly it regarded this same matter in canon
passages.notes: 'This day' is Thursday (feria quinta), the day of Jupiter. The canon number (15) follows in the next context.

passages.original: Rhelicium (inquit S. Augustinus), ab Augustoduno episcopum, magnæ fuisse auctoritatis in Ecclesia tempore episcopatus sui, gesta illa ecclesiastica, nobis indicant, quando in urbe Roma, Melchiade apostolicæ sedis; episcopo præsidente, cum aliis judex interfuit, Donatumque damnavit, qui prior auctor Donatistarum schismatis fuit, et Cæcilianum, episcopum Ecclesiae Carthaginensis, absolvit. Is, cum de baptismo ageret, ita locutus est:
passages.english: "That Reticius," says St Augustine, "bishop of Autun, was of great authority in the Church in the time of his episcopate, those ecclesiastical acts show us, when in the city of Rome, with Melchiades, bishop of the apostolic see, presiding, he took part as a judge with others, and condemned Donatus, who was the first author of the Donatist schism, and acquitted Caecilian, bishop of the church of Carthage. He, when he was treating of baptism, spoke thus:
passages.notes: 'Rhelicium' read as Reticius (Rheticius), bishop of Autun.
